negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin bank was found publishing a document explicitly branded 'Stub 3' / 'Pillar 3'. The equivalent artefact is published under the local term 'javno objelodanjivanje/objavljivanje podataka i informacija' with a reference date, citing the Law on Credit Institutions and CBCG disclosure regulation.
negative_findings.result_summary: The seed query 'godišnji izvještaj banke Crna Gora objelodanjivanje Stub 3' returned only EBA/BIS/Canadian/Maltese Pillar 3 material and no ME bank document; the local-term query returned the real artefacts (Addiko, CKB, Prva banka).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collectors keyed on 'Pillar 3'/'Stub 3' will miss the entire Montenegrin disclosure corpus. Query templates must use 'objelodanjivanje podataka' / 'objavljivanje podataka i informacija' instead.

negative_findings.description: https://www.ckb.me/ could not be fetched: TLS error 'unable to verify the first certificate'.
negative_findings.result_summary: Root fetch failed on certificate chain, while document URLs on the same host (opsti-uslovi PDFs, tarifnik, 2024 auditor report) appeared in search results, so the site is almost certainly live with an incomplete intermediate chain.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The market-leading bank must not be recorded as dead. The collector for ckb.me needs a fetcher tolerant of chain issues (or a full CA bundle), and CBCG's mirror is the fallback for its financial statements.

negative_findings.description: Homepage fetches of nlb.me, erstebank.me, lovcenbanka.me and prvabankacg.com surfaced only product marketing; none exposed a discoverable, dated 'obavještenja za klijente' archive to the fetcher.
negative_findings.result_summary: Four of the largest banks' homepages returned no notice-index URL; notice content appears to live in JS-rendered news carousels or one-off PDF links rather than a stable archive.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Customer notices are the earliest evidence signal in this cell, and for most banks they are not archived at a stable URL — a snapshot-and-diff collector (or headless rendering) is required rather than a simple RSS/index crawl, and historical notices may be unrecoverable.

negative_findings.description: Local-language queries strongly pull in same-brand entities from BiH and Serbia (asabanka.ba, nlb-rs.ba, nlbkb.rs, addiko.rs, adriaticbank.rs) whose notices use nearly identical wording.
negative_findings.result_summary: Several top hits for 'obavijest/obavještenje o izmjeni opštih uslova' were Bosnian or Serbian banks, not Montenegrin ones.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any collector must hard-filter on Montenegrin domains/entity names, otherwise the cell will be polluted with out-of-jurisdiction notices that look authentic. 'Obavijest' (BiH/HR spelling) vs 'obavještenje' (ME/RS) is a useful discriminator but not sufficient.

negative_findings.description: The routine playbook at C:/Users/User/Dropbox/... is a Windows path and does not exist on this macOS host; method was applied from the task brief only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Classification vocabulary and scoring calibration may drift from the canonical routine definition.

coverage_gaps.description: Four licensed banks (Universal Capital Bank, Zapad banka, Ziraat Bank Montenegro, Adriatic Bank) were enumerated from the CBCG directory but their disclosure/terms sections were not located this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a per-domain site crawl for the paths 'opsti-uslovi', 'tarifnik', 'naknade', 'objelodanjivanje', 'izvjestaji' on ucbank.me, zapadbanka.me, ziraatbank.me, adriaticbank.com and register the exact URLs.

coverage_gaps.description: No bank was found publishing a standalone compliance/regulatory statement (e.g. AML, sanctions, DORA/PSD2-equivalent readiness, ESG/CSRD compliance) as a distinct document, beyond privacy notices and codes of conduct.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Targeted search per bank for 'izjava o usklađenosti', 'politika usklađenosti', 'sprječavanje pranja novca', 'AML politika', 'izjava o korporativnom upravljanju'.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language mirrors exist for at least NLB (/en/) and several banks, but no systematic check was made of whether EN mirrors carry the same notices as the SR pages.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Sample-compare SR vs EN versions of terms/notice pages for 3 banks; if EN lags, mark SR as the authoritative capture language for the whole cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Historical versions of general terms and fee tariffs are typically overwritten; banks publish only the currently applicable version, so the change history that evidences notice periods is not natively retrievable.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Stand up a snapshot store from now on (hash + effective date per PDF) and backfill where possible from web archives; do not rely on the banks retaining prior versions.

coverage_gaps.description: This cell was scoped to banks; payment institutions, e-money institutions and MFIs licensed by CBCG have parallel notice/disclosure duties and were not covered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend enumeration from the CBCG registers of payment institutions and e-money institutions in a follow-up cell.

brief: Montenegro's eleven licensed banks are all obliged publishers, but their output splits into two very different collection problems. Structured, archived disclosure — annual reports, auditor reports and 'javno objelodanjivanje podataka' filed under the Law on Credit Institutions — is reliably available both on bank sites (Addiko is the model archive; CKB, Erste, Prva banka, Hipotekarna comparable) and, crucially, mirrored by CBCG in a uniform per-year path scheme that guarantees complete comparable coverage. Customer notices on general-terms and fee-tariff changes, which are the earliest evidence that a rule or deadline is biting, are far weaker as sources: only Hipotekarna and NLB expose clearly dated terms/tariff pages, most banks publish notices in transient homepage carousels with no stable archive, and prior versions are overwritten — so a snapshot-and-diff collector plus CBCG's cross-bank 'Tarife banaka' comparison is the workable design. Note the local vocabulary trap: 'Pillar 3 / Stub 3' returns nothing Montenegrin, while 'objelodanjivanje/objavljivanje podataka i informacija' returns the whole corpus, and Bosnian/Serbian same-brand sites contaminate every local-language query.
